More than 20 years ago, when I was only a little

That hot summer when FFX was released

FF and Dragon Quest, so to speak

My father likes Square and Enix games

A room with freezing air conditioning and the smell of cigarettes

The father is doing FFX while smoking there

Next to such a father

Me: If you go this way, you can get something, right? ( Items and treasure chests)

Father "Okay! Then, let's go there!

At that time, the two of us were moving forward while saying that. I still remember it vividly

At that time, I was young and couldn't understand the content, but I was gnawing on the TV screen with my favorite father who was playing my favorite game.

I'm already in my late 20s

Play again as an adult

I realized that it was a very moving and hot game.

At the same time, nostalgia is fulfilled.

Life is too fast and too short lol

Please live a little longer, Dad.

I'm going to toast with my father today

With love from Japan

stories.author: @Codemaster92163
stories.text:
This song has a new association for me, now. 

I would play through FFX every few years or so, and on my most recent playthrough, I lost my cat. Not just A cat, but one of the sweetest, most affectionate and wonderful animals I've ever had the pleasure of owning. She went missing and never came back, right towards the end of my most recent playthrough. And not missing as in someone else got her, but missing as in we're pretty certain wild coy dogs got her.

It was a really difficult time, but oddly enough, the themes of the game and the challenges they all deal with helped to ground me and remind myself that death is just a part of life. Everyone in that game lost someone, and they kept going, so it helped remind me that I'd be alright and move on with my grief. 

So, this song made me cry today when listening. I don't know if I'll ever be able to play the game again, because anything in it reminds me of her, but I will always love it and appreciate how it helped me cope with death, even if some people don't consider the death of a beloved pet as significant.

stories.author: @letalleurkevin5133
stories.text:
It was 2001. I was 11 years old. You can't imagine just how mind-blowing that opening scene was. The console gaming market was entering its golden age; competition was fierce, but when SquareSoft released Final Fantasy X, they completely obliterated the competition. A colleague's older brother was working at Ubisoft on a game called Beyond Good & Evil. When Square dropped the trailer featuring that cinematic, there was dead silence in the studio the next day. Everyone was stunned by the sheer technical leap. Their game was due out at the end of the year. They ended up starting almost from scratch because the release of FFX had rendered two years of their work graphically obsolete. They weren't the only ones, either; some studios had to completely change their approach to game design. Final Fantasy X thus marked the beginning of the "graphics arms race... a trend that, unfortunately, led to a homogenization of design by the end of the 2000s.

It’s crazy to think just how unrivaled Square was in the early 2000s (to the point where even Disney tried to piggyback on their hype) and then to see how they managed to squander the gold mine they were sitting on. There’s a parallel universe where SquareSoft acquires Marvel in 2008 and Star Wars in 2013, and where the PlayStation 5 is called the "SquareStation 2" following a merger with Sony in 2006. Even though Square remains one of the biggest studios, it pales in comparison to what they could have become had it not been for a cascade of bad decisions. Any other company would have gone under long ago. In that sense, the existence of the FFVII Remake trilogy is nothing short of a miracle...

I was in a coffee shop, running away from home when I heard the news; our hero, Jecht.  
Gone. Vanished into thin air. 

My dad must have been his biggest fan. 
I knew how sad he'd be. Heck we all were that day.
'Zanar' I says to myself  'what are you thinking?'
I went running straight back home. 
We sat up talking 'bout Jecht all night.
 My dad and I never talked so much. 
Whoa... Didn't mean to reminisce folks.

Anyway, ten years later, the Jecht Memorial Cup Tournament is today! 
The two teams that have won through to the finals are of course the Abes
 from A-East and the Duggles from C-South. I know there's a lot of people 
out there today to see the star of the Abes! In just one year, he's become
 the team's number one player! He's Jecht's blood and the new hope of blitzball!
 What kind of super play will he show us today? Will we see his father's 
legendary shot? I don't think I'm the only one excited here folks!

stories.author: @Mythiiks

"I was in a coffee shop, running away from home when I heard the news."
"Our hero, Jecht, gone, vanished into thin air!"
"My dad must have been his biggest fan. I knew how sad he'd be. Heck, we all were that day."
""Zanar," I says to myself, "What are you thinking?""
"I went running straight back home. We sat up talking 'bout Jecht all night."
"My dad and I never talked so much. Whoa... Didn't mean to reminisce, folks."
"Anyways... Ten years later, the Jecht Memorial Cup tournament is today!"
"The two teams that have won through to the finals are...of course, the Abes from A-East and the Duggles from C-South."
"I know there's a lot of people out there today to see the star of the Abes!"
"In just one year, he's become the team's number one player!"
"He's Jecht's blood, and the new hope of blitzball! What kind of super play will he show us today?"
"Will we see his father's legendary shot? I don't think I'm the only one excited here, folks!"

stories.author: @N三UROMANCER
stories.text: This was the first metal song I ever heard with vocals like this. It was revolutionary, esp for me as a kid. I was about 10 or 11 when this came out. Never heard metal like this before. and I was into black sabbath and stuff my brother listened to. But this set me on a diverted path. I began to explore more punk, then eventually grindcore crust, which eventually lead me back to death metal. This song feels like death metal. I have been looking for tropical metal band since then to capture the feeling of FF10. Remake this game next SQUARE!!! I want to play a action based blitzball match while this song plays!!

stories.author: @ultimuh
stories.text:
I just recently beat FFX after buying it back in 2016. I was not a fan of RPGs back then so i have no idea why I was compelled to buy it other than I needed games for the brand new PS4 I got.

Even as someone who didn’t like RPGs back then, there was something about this game that kind of clicked for me. After a while I played other RPG’s and started liking the genre a bit more and more and eventually I went back to beat this game. 

I started to play other final fantasy games because of this game being my introduction to the series. Usually I attribute Earthbound to being the RPG that got me into the genre, but I think if not for this game I wouldn’t have even bothered. 

I would consider buying this game the weirdest choice I don’t ever really regret.

stories.author: @theloz3r
stories.text: I kinda associate this song with the last points of my life I was still positive of my future, which was January of 2018. I had saved up enough money to buy this game on PS4. When I got it, and mainly this part of the game I couldn’t help but just sit there and listen to it. It was so calming and melancholic at the same time. But then things in my personal life went very awry, like not even a month later, and kinda started a continuous struggle with depression. Keep in mind i was only like 13, but in a weird way, this song now seems like the last song of my childhood innocence, in a way. I’ve had to deal with a lot of shit since I’ve been born, but I still had a sense of optimism. It’s crazy how music can be intrinsically tied with emotional moments of your life, but that’s the power of music, wether it’s good or bad, it can bring us back in time to moments that can forever change how you are and what that can lead to.

stories.text: My brother and I were adopted by a great man after a childhood hell. He had a PS2 and gamed with us back in the day. In 2001 we all got this, and played it to death. stories.author: @seanturner1197
stories.text:
This was my first ps2 game, I never forgot the joy I felt when dad showed me the case, way back in 2002 when I was picked up from school.
Couldn't finish it though, not without a game save from a ps2 magazine demo.
I have since obtained the steam version.
And am close to finishing it.
Close; I am having fun, trouncing the dark aeons as payback Time.

stories.author: @yyoksetioxd
stories.text: This one and "people from the far north" are my favorite tracks from FFX, but this one perfectly captures the essence of final fantasy. There are some tracks that you just know "this is from Uematsu and it's from a Final Fantasy", no matter if it's the first time you listen to it. PS3/PS4/PS5 FF titles lost this magic. Don't get me wrong, they have great OSTs, but they don't have the ¿magic? the PS1 and PS2 OSTs had.

stories.author: @IcyAuron
stories.text: I know that a bunch of songs in the soundtrack use Suteki da ne as a leitmotif, but I've ALWAYS thought that this song never got nearly enough attention. It's the best of them, and it's one of the main character's theme, for crying out loud!

stories.author: @AsimSiddiqui007
stories.text:
Listening to this after more than a decade, drown by emotions of my parents who both left me in 2023. My elder sister was my second mofher. I loved her and spent on her, all the money I could earn, and she abandoned me to live with my elder brother just because he is mentally stronger and can support her better.

I have been crying for about half an hour with such agony, hoping that my 4 cats would understand, but it looks like they don't.

I miss my mummy so much.. Always dream of her.. Heart does not stop aching. This track unleashed my emotions that lay within, me unaware of them.. I miss mummy so much. I wish she could know how much I miss her and pray for her..

stories.author: @keeganstormblade5456
stories.text:
Tidus: Who are you, anyway? You knew my old man, didn’t you?
Auron: Yeah.
Tidus: And you also knew Yuna’s father?
Auron: That’s correct.
Tidus: Hey, man, there’s no way. That’s just impossible.
Auron: Nothing impossible about it. Jecht, Braska and I… Together we defeated Sin ten years ago. Then I went to Zanarkand… where I watched over you. So that one day I could bring you to Spira.
Tidus: Why did it have to be me?
Auron: Jecht asked me to.
Tidus: Is he alive?
Auron: It depends on what you mean by “alive.” He is no longer human. But then… I felt something of Jecht, there in that shell… couldn’t you? You must have felt him when you came in contact with Sin.

stories.author: @lukeferguson9236
stories.text: I never finished FFX-II. I didn't like the concept of turning a somber prestress into a music idol or how sexualized the three main characters were, despite Rikku still being underaged. Everything about it was just weird. However, I always thought that they should do a prequel with Jecht, Braska, and Auron. That would have slapped, and every time I hear this theme, I'm reminded of what could of been.

stories.text: I've always loved this track for its contrast between the chill and relaxing music and the dangerous, stormy place where it plays, but now I love it even more after finally completing the 200-lightning challenge right during the FFX stream last July. stories.author: @keeganstormblade5456
stories.text:
"Hey. If you’re sitting there, watching this…it means you’re stuck in Spira, like me. You might not know when you’ll get back home, but you better not be crying! Although, I guess I’d understand. But you know what? There’s a time when you have to stop crying and move on. You’ll be fine. Remember, you’re my son. And… Well, uh… Never mind. I’m no good at these things."

"Anyways… I believe in you. Be good. Goodbye."

stories.author: @FiendMatadorSlayerOfNoobs
stories.text:
Man, oh man. I was 10 years old when I got to this, on a snowy, lit up December in 2001- My cousin had bought a PS2 and 3 games: Wrath of Cortex, Sons of Liberty, and Final Fantasy X.

I was a scrawny little kid from a non-English speaking country, who pieced together what little my brain could just from context, events and associating certain phrases & words, and my really badly-managed Sphere Grid..


But dang, this music made me bawl from how beautiful it was. My father legit thought I had hurt myself while playing. I still remember how he had this small laugh before he gave me a big hug during the violin part and asked me if the "movie" was sad.

Heh, he was awestruck when I told him it was a video game. After that, he would sit down and watch me play on occasion, and since he actually could speak an okay amount of English, he would translate stuff I didn't understand in the cutscenes. Shit, I love my childhood.

stories.author: @Kalendil
stories.text: I never, ever thought that I could cry over a game until I played FFX. I was 25 years old when I was able to bought my own PS2 (13 years ago). Because I loved Fanatasy, I bought that game... and it was INCREDIBLE. The story, de sound, the animations... I was in love with the game.  And at the end... I couldn't stop crying. I remembered that when I started to figure Tidus's fate out I was like: no, no, no no no no NO! COME ON! It broke my heart. How I wish this story turned out in a book or a movie so I can treasure it forever.

stories.author: @tutuvue6294
stories.text:
Played this game when I was 11 years old..it felt so ahead of its time. Voice acting, cinematics, all of that. It felt like I was stuck in this world just as tidus was, growing attached to every character and hating villains like seymour and sin.

When the story concluded it was very sad and beautiful even for a kid like me. One of the greatest experience of my life still to this day.

In a blink of an eye, I’ll turn 30 and then 35… but the feelings will remain in my heart

stories.author: @YungFuggi
stories.text:
27 right now, and I had never played it before. As I’m writing this, the credits are rolling. I’ve spent hundreds of hours in the HD version and did EVERYTHING, including going for the Platinum. But since I wanted to actually enjoy the game, and damn, I’m crying because it’s going to be such a beautiful memory. Being part of this little world of its own was something really special.

Wow, the way the credits immediately transition back to the main menu with the game’s soundtrack playing is beautiful.

Btw, after this I’m finally going to properly play Kingdom Hearts for the first time. I only had Kingdom Hearts II as a kid, but I never actually finished it xD Another journey awaits me.

stories.author: @しょっくん-w7x
stories.text:
SUTEKI DANE / RIKKI

【Verse 1】
Words the wind carried in,
my heart drifted along.
Voices leaping with hope
for tomorrow the clouds will bring.

In the moonlit mirror,
my trembling heart sways.
As the stars fall away,
soft tears spill down my face.

Wouldn’t it be wonderful…
if we could somehow walk hand in hand,
I’d want to go
to your town, your home, into your arms.

I’ll lay myself on your chest,
lose myself in the dusk,
and dream.


【Verse 2】
The wind falls still,
and words fade into gentle illusions.
The clouds break apart,
and tomorrow becomes a distant voice.

My heart drifts through
a mirror blurred by the moon.
As the stars tremble,
tears I can’t hide spill over.

Wouldn’t it be wonderful…
if we could somehow walk hand in hand,
I’d want to go
to your town, your home, into your arms.

I’d softly reach out
and touch your face,
melting into the morning,
and dream.

stories.author: @CinemaSquad89
stories.text:
Hi, Rinoabelle.
It’s been seven years since we last saw each other.
This was our last song while cruising down the road, with you resting on my lap.

I know you have a family now. I’m sorry for how things ended back then. I just want you to know that I’m always proud of you, and I’m happy for where you are now.

Who would’ve thought that would be our last moment, right?

Thank you for the beautiful memories

stories.author: @AspiePilo82
stories.text:
Never beat the game.
 I bought the game when it first came out. Was very excited. Played it and got to the final part. I decided to do side quests before fighting Sin.
I then visited a friend, and this guy spoils the ending without me asking. I felt so devastated and disgusted that I refused to keep playing the game, felt that an experience and moment was taken from me.
Well its been over 20 years now and on the journey of playing the game again after I'm done with some of the earlier Final Fantasy titles. 
I have to find conclusion with this game. Its going to be weird me saying this, but I don't want to pass away before finishing this game. 
Every time i see a FFX clip or hear this song it makes me cry.

stories.author: @dizzitoast
stories.text:
Not a true translation. But poetic reinterpretation:

Words carried by the wind
set my heart adrift.

Tomorrow, borne on the clouds,
made my voice leap with hope.

In the mirror where the moon trembles,
my heart quivered.

As the stars flowed and spilled,
soft tears fell.

⸻

Isn’t it beautiful?

If only the two of us
could walk hand in hand.

I want to go…

to your town,

your home,

into your arms.

⸻

There,

I rest my body

against your heart,

hidden within the evening,

dreaming.

⸻

The wind grows still.

The words become

a gentle illusion.

The clouds break apart.

Tomorrow

becomes a distant voice.

⸻

The mirror blurred by the moon

carries away my heart.

The stars tremble,

overflowing—

tears

I can no longer hide.

⸻

Isn’t it beautiful?

If only the two of us
could walk hand in hand.

I want to go…

to your town,

your home,

into your arms.

⸻

To gently touch

your face…

dreaming

until the dream melts

into the morning.

Written by one Japanese man


Words borne on the wind,
my heart drifted.

Toward tomorrow on the clouds,
my voice leapt.

In a mirror trembling with the moon,
my heart quivered.

As stars streamed by,
soft tears spilled.

How lovely it would be
if we could walk hand in hand.

I wish I could go
to your town, your home, your arms.

Against your heart,
lost in the dusk,
I dream.

stories.author: @cloudxz92
stories.text:
My dad died when I was 10 years old on December 7, 2002. 
On December 24th my grandma brought me a PS2, and my first game was Final Fantasy 10. 
I was still in grief, but it was getting better a little bit at least I tought so.
When the group was in the Farplane, this song played, and Lulu said, "He is dead, and I am still alive." This was the first time I really let everything that was inside me for 3 Weeks out, and it helped me so much. 
I can't explain it anymore, but it was the first time I felt better and something like peace. I know he was gone, but somehow it felt like he was still close. I was 10 at that time.
Final Fantasy 10 helped me a lot back then. How can a Child understand that his Dad will never comes back. I could not and FF10 gave me something like a Answer back then.

stories.author: @museyip815
stories.text:
The “Ending Theme” of FINAL FANTASY X is absolutely stunning and beautiful. Whenever I listen to it and watch the wonderful scenes that it is forever associated with, I always find myself in tears. Several years ago, after my dad’s passing in 2014, my mom and I listened to this track together for the first time. We were very moved by it. Listening to it somehow helped us to heal together after the tragedy that we had endured. Therefore, the “Ending Theme” always made, and continues to cause, me to think of him. So many great memories came back to me during the ensuing years. After my mom later passed away due to cancer in October of 2023, listening to the “Ending Theme” allowed me to begin to heal while thinking of them. My parents were my first best friends and my caregivers during their lifetimes. I am a wheelchair user who has a cerebral palsy diagnosis. To this day, it brings back memories of them whenever I listen to the “Ending Theme”. Their smiles; their laughter; their love; their wisdom; their joy; and much more are among those memories. Today (January 19th of 2026) marks more than 2 years since my mom’s passing. There is not a day that goes by without letting me think of her and my dad. My journey, ever since their departures from this world, has been very difficult. But, somehow, I find the courage to continue to do my best to keep their legacy alive and to live a fulfilling life in their memory. Even though “the journey will be hard”,  which  is what Yuna says after the credits  in the English-language version of FINAL FANTASY X, I will be able to live such a life because of my parents’ memory; the love that they shared with me; and the kind-hearted people who are in my life. This is what I continue to hope for. I pray that my parents will continue to bless me and protect me from beyond. 

Hi, Mom. Hi, Dad. I  love you very much and I miss you every day. There’s not a day that goes by without listening to me speak about wanting you to come back to me. There’s not a day that goes by without letting me have courage as I think of you and try to do my best each day. Every beautiful memory I have of you is a blessing and a portal to wonderful dimensions. Thank you for everything that you have given, and continue to give, to me. Even though my journey has been, and will be, difficult, I promise to continue to do my best. I promise to never forget to smile. Love you, Mom. Love you, Dad. May you continue to be at peace now, forever, and always. You remain in my heart, and will continue to have sanctuaries in it. Please continue to guide, protect, and bless me by way of your love. I will see you again.❤🙏🏻

Yuna’s courage; Tidus’ reconciliation with Jecht; the love that Yuna and Tidus share; as well as the beautiful soundtrack of FINAL FANTASY X are among the many things that I will always remember about this game, even though I have never played it before. 

Blessings to everyone who made FINAL FANTASY X possible and to everyone who continues to preserve its  marvelous legacy. 

I send my love to all of you as someone who is trying to brighten my future while cherishing my memories and cherishing the goodness of each day that I experience. I am someone who is searching for my own Zanarkand. My own haven of dreams. I pray that I will find it someday. 

Best wishes from New York City, 
Muse Yip

One of the most heartwrenching endings in any videogame and thank god that they didn't play the actual cutscene along with the song because in that case the channel would have been even more flooded with tears.
Back in the days before FFX-2 this was, along with FFVII, the only FF game that didn't have a happy ending, but, personally, I think this is much harder to accept because VII gives you basically half the game to process Aerith's death, whereas here tragedy strikes literally at the last moment. Thankfully the sequel has changed everything for the better🥰.


Ah, a curious fact: this is one of the few cases in which the dubbed version is even more heartbreaking than the og because, if i recall correctly, Yuna's "I love you" was not in the japanese script (if i'm wrong feel free to correct me, japanese fans🙏).

stories.author: @しょっくん-w7x
stories.text:
SUTEKI DANE / RIKKI

【Verse 1】
Words the wind carried in,
my heart drifted along.
Voices leaping with hope
for tomorrow the clouds will bring.

In the moonlit mirror,
my trembling heart sways.
As the stars fall away,
soft tears spill down my face.

Wouldn’t it be wonderful…
if we could somehow walk hand in hand,
I’d want to go
to your town, your home, into your arms.

I’ll lay myself on your chest,
lose myself in the dusk,
and dream.


【Verse 2】
The wind falls still,
and words fade into gentle illusions.
The clouds break apart,
and tomorrow becomes a distant voice.

My heart drifts through
a mirror blurred by the moon.
As the stars tremble,
tears I can’t hide spill over.

Wouldn’t it be wonderful…
if we could somehow walk hand in hand,
I’d want to go
to your town, your home, into your arms.

I’d softly reach out
and touch your face,
melting into the morning,
and dream.

stories.author: @Fujikawa-hw6ij
stories.text:
This track has a warm place in my heart for so many reasons. The biggest reason for being the song that makes me smile and sad at the same time.

My uncle died when my two little nieces where very young. It messed the oldest one up pretty bad. Me, my sister, nephew and other nieces are very different people but we have this one thing in common. Kingdom Hearts. So we played it with each other,, mostly me playing and then just watching and experiencing this game together. 

Sad to say that a few years later my aunt , the mother of two other nieces and a nephew passed from lung cancer. We all went back to my house, dusted off the PS2 and listened to this song for about 30 min and just played, and played.

We have a pact now, since most of us are caught up in adult life, to meet each other at least one day a year, guess what we talk about. When KH3 came out some of us couldn’t make it so we streamed for each other on launch day.

My niece from, the first one I talked about is still not doing well, poor thing. But listing to this song together, and when iam alone brings a tear in my eye while also smiling. We cherish the ones we lost and loved, and cherish the ones who are still here with us. It makes me remember we are not alone, and like sora I try to see or find the good in everything around me.

He who tells me videogames are not art, is sadly mistaken. And KH2 was a pure masterpiece.

stories.author: @mysteriousfigure5996
stories.text:
This game is so special to me. Everytime I boot up KH2, my late brother was always watching me play, like he was my only audience behind me while playing KH2. Thanks to this game our bond became so much stronger. Not until he passed away few years ago, his death hit me hard to the point I lost interest in this series. I tried avoiding things that made me remember him, including avoiding playing KH because it reminds me of him. Because everytime I remember that he's gone and he will never be my audience again while playing KH, I feel so depressed. 

Until KH4 was announced, I was so happy and excited for the upcoming game! My love for this series came back eventually. The more I avoid things that makes me remember him, the more it comes back at me naturally. I feel like my brother's spirit still lingers in me and still guides me wherever I go. The memories we had with this game is the one keeps me moving forward. When I heard this song for the first time again I teared up.

stories.author: @Darkfrost815
stories.text:
I once wondered if I would ever find someone in this world to spend the rest of my life with. Often times I came to the conclusion that I was going to die alone, and I had become alright with that. This song helped me stay calm in very difficult times, and it saved me in many ways. My childhood with this song in it is one of the greatest things I could have ever dreamed of.

Then, 2 and a half years ago, I met my wife. Since the day I met her, my life changed. She has been the best thing to have ever happen to me, and I can finally say I've found my soulmate. Listening to this song has me in tears, because of the overwhelming amount of joy she has brought into my life. I will always love her, and my life will always be better just because she is in it.

Alejandra, I love you with every fiber of my being. Thank you for making my life perfect with just your presence.

stories.author: @caspenknight7464
stories.text:
Kingdom hearts holds a special place in my childhood.
Not only was it a game i spent hours on alone. It was a bounding moment between my siblings and me. I spent a lot of time asking my older brother for help on KH1, especially in Alice's world.
After a while i struggled my way to that Malificent Dragon.
I didn't want to ask for help this time, I was determined. 
I was also on a time limit because my brother was going on deployment soon into the Navy.
In was fighting her while he was getting ready desperately trying to win in time. I had to pause and say good bye to him. I beat her shortly after he left. My brother and I just aren't as close anymore, and i just miss those days.

Kingdom Hearts 2 is where i really bonded with my older sister. I remember helping her with the more skill based challenges, while she helped me with figuring out what to do next. We spent a lot of time together, but in more recent years we didn't talk anymore. I don't know if it was due to mental illness or not, but she thinks everything i do is to spite her. While I really do love my sister and want what is best for her. I don't know how to have her in my life in a positive way, and I don't have the tools to help her. Even still I've tried, and only done more damage to our relationship. I just miss my sister.




Sorry I had nowhere else to dump this.

stories.author: @Salted_Neko
stories.text:
Around June 2021 I decided to get and play kingdom hearts since I was little and watched my older brother play kh1. When I got the hd remix of 1 and 2, I was hooked on the series, watching theory videos, reciting the weird lore to my friends, and even buying some merchandise. I soon after got Kh3 and its re:mind dlc, and I love the games for different reasons.
Kh1 for the slight nostalgic feeling it gave me the whole game
Kh2 for its combat, story, music, one of my favorite villains “XEMNAS”, and Roxas as a character(especially loved how he was in 358/2 days)
BBS just felt really fun to play.
And Kh3+re:mind for its flashiness, I ESPECIALLY love the vfx for the “Thundaza” spell, and the finishers for “Ultimate Form” and “Double form”. Also around that time, I had begun slow, but steady progress working on a video game I’ve thought of making since I was little. I was thinking about how combat would work, then I saw the interesting combos of KH2, and Kh3 and went “Yeah, that’s what I’ll base it off of!”. Now on another note, you may notice I didn’t mention KH re:coded or Chain of Memories. I frankly just didn’t care for re:coded, and I didn’t really have much fun with chain of memories. The whole card system while fighting a boss and freely moving felt so weird to me, and the thing I didn’t like the most was castle oblivion and the grinding I had to do in order to get past a certain door. That said, I know COM is a good game, but its combat and the late game grinding was just not for me, though i do like how it bridged the ending of kh1, to the start of kh2. Now when I’m with my mother, I sometimes play the kh2 rendition of dearly beloved because it’s so calming along with BBS's rendition, genuinely made me tear up from its beauty. This comment I just wrote within 10 minutes will likely be ignored, but I don’t care, I at least wanted to comment this to show my love for the series as a whole, even the weird bits. For those of you who may give this a like or even reply with something nice, thank you so much. This is the consumer of salt, signing off

stories.author: @juliuskresnik198
stories.text:
It's odd, to be filled with such Nostalgia so early in life. You hear so often as you grow up of how it'll feel, traces of experience, muddled with time and yet fondly remembered nonetheless. 

The melancholy, I didn't expect it tonight.

But, I have so much more life to live. I'm only 22. Recently diagnosed and medicated for a disorder I'd only heard about a year ago. Things make sense now, I feel in control like never before.

And yet, I look back here, this music thawing my disjointed memories and reminding me of the person I was. I see that kid, lost and scared, stumbling about in the dark on his own despite knowing deep down something was wrong. 

He didn't give up. It came close a few times, it really did but at every opportunity, he chose to be better. To be that stubborn little bastard he'd seen on TV and Video Games.

And now, I lay here at night, turning to the next chapter.

I'm learning to drive again, learning to relax, got a new job and I've even got a tentative plan for the future, even if it means starting over again. I'm still that kid but I wouldn't be where I am without the little guy who found peace in this Title Screen, in this game.

The past fills me with a soft sorrow and a warm peace in equal measure, and yet the future calls out to me, the future that little kid had always wanted. I'll take it in both hands and make him proud. I'll add to this collection of disjointed memories. I'll add the laughter, joy, love, excitement, pain, peace and perseverance of a lifetime as the man I've always wanted to be.

I still remember the exact moment I bought this game. It was a used copy in a GameStop and I had never heard of the game before, but the cover and pictures looked really cool to me. Turns out that was the day that I bought my favourite game of all time.
Played through it so many times and often left the main menu open just to listen to this.
The amount of nostalgia I feel when hearing this nowadays is honestly overwhelming and makes me tear up instantly. I wish I could go back to this exact moment of my life and relive all of it for the first time again. I miss waking up in the morning and not having to worry about anything. It truly was the simplest and best time of my life. Thank you to everyone in Square Enix for creating this wonderful game and Yoko Shimomura for composing the most beautiful piece of music. Nothing will ever top this for me.

stories.author: @marcomillan3749
stories.text:
Dear Kingdom Hearts,

I'm writing to express my deepest gratitude for everything you've done for me. When I was a kid, I was bullied and felt like I didn't have any friends. But then I discovered your game, and everything changed.

Through your story and characters, I learned about the power of friendship and the importance of believing in myself. I felt like I was part of something bigger than myself, and that gave me the strength to keep going.

I can't even imagine where I would be today if I hadn't found you. You showed me that no matter how dark things may seem, there's always hope. You gave me a reason to believe in myself and the people around me.

So thank you, from the bottom of my heart. Thank you for saving my life and showing me the true power of friendship.

Sincerely,

Me ❤

stories.author: @CherishedJoysASMR
stories.text:
This game was my escape daydream 24/7, even when not playing. It literally saved my child and teenage self, along with my only friend. Countless nights falling asleep crying, with this song being my lullaby and a hope for better days coming. 
I'm turning 27 this year. Being suicidal, never thought back then I would make it so far. I wanted to unalive myself while listening to this, to finally find peace and be free. 
Now here I am, having not played any of the games for years, as an adult, listening to this. Echoing of times long gone.. I'm crying again.. But it feels cathartic now. All my selves are crying, but the little ones are not alone and scared anymore. 

Dearly beloved indeed. Thank you Yoko Shimomura 🤍

"A scattered dream that's like a far-off memory... a far-off memory that's like a scattered dream... i want to line the pieces up... yours and mine."

stories.author: @SylumSolosEverything
stories.text:
The real name of this song is called "The Other Promise." There are TONS of different renditions of this song in the series and it's one of the most popular soundtracks in the franchise. This version is just one of them...

Correct me if I'm wrong,, but I believe this specific rendition only plays once in the whole franchise and that is in the beginning of Kingdom Hearts II during the cutscene when Roxas discovers the truth of his existence...that he is not actually his own person; that he is just a husk -- a remnant left behind after Sora temporarily became a Heartless in the first game -- and that the town he thought he grew up in was just a simulation -- a datascape which he was imprisoned into with fake memories and fake friends created for the purpose of being studied by someone he's never met. The most heart-wrenching part of this whole thing was the pure existential despair over the sudden realization that he was never a real person and that he was never even meant to exist to begin with. Not to forget that his friends weren't even real and their real-life counterparts have no idea who he even is. The existential dread of not only his existence being an accident and knowing that he isn't even his own individual but some scrap left behind by someone he doesn't know but the fact that the place that he loved and the people he cared dearly about weren't even real. What mattered dearly to him was in reality just someone else's disposable data.

I was like 11 or 12 or something when I played KHII for the first time... which was actually the very first Kingdom Hearts game I've ever played. It was a weird beginning to be introduced into the franchise, but I remember being just as confused and crushed as Roxas was when he discovered Sora in his sleeping pod. (The fact that Roxas was just as clueless to Sora's identity as I was only poured gas onto the fire.) I nearly wanted to just quit the game after that. The sudden turn in tone from that dark intro to Soras bright and positive adventurous attitude felt uncanny, especially considering that I knew ZERO background to the franchise back then.

stories.author: @korggg123
stories.text:
Unlike many who played KH1 before KH2, KH2 was my first KH game. So when I first started KH2, I didn't have any emotional connection to KH1's main character, Sora. Roxas was my first KH main character and thought that Roxas would be the main character for the rest of the game. I was an early teenager attending middle school back then, and to me Roxas was a cool looking character with spiky blonde hair with emo-like personality.

After hours of playing the game, I felt a strong bond with Roxas as well as his friends in the Twilight Town. But then, the story continued and I came to realize that all the hours spent progressing the story and developing relationships with friends were all fake and artificially generated. I have never felt so much disappointment and emptiness. All the effort and memories were in vain. 

And when Roxas encountered sleeping Sora followed by a sudden shift in the main character to Sora with 'bright, optimistic' soundtrack, I did not know what was going on. 
In my head, I was confused, asking countless questions... 
Who is this boy? Who's Sora? What happened to Roxas? I am still processing what is going on. Give me a break. I still care about Roxas and his pain. What was his purpose? What happened to his existence? Will I ever meet Roxas again? 
 
The sudden departure from my old friend and getting replaced with a new one was very odd and uncomfortable for me at that time. I was all confused as I could not catch up with the pacing of the story. At that time, I have never played KH1, so I did not have any emotional connection to Sora and his friends.  
(At least for people who played KH1 would be like "You are finally back! Good to see you! Btw, do you know where Roxas go?")
 
I was still thinking about Roxas's anger and despair, but without given any time to process that pain, it felt like I was being shove down my throat with optimistic soundtrack and a 'new adventure vibe'. And without given sufficient time to process emotion, I just had to play along with the storyline. 

Well... as story went on, I gradually forgot about Roxas and felt more connection with Sora. And when I finally encountered Roxas again towards the end of the story, it was like seeing my old friend, with whom I shared bittersweet memories, again after years. We both know we shared great memories but also know we both have changed so much that we can't go back to good old days (first meeting at the start of KH2). 

Anyway, it's this experience with Roxas that was most memorable in the franchise. The developers did a great job narrating the story. Instead of jumping right off to Sora, they found a clever way to introduce a new character and at the same time, make people like that character. 

"...looks like my summer vacation is...over..."
This quote along with Roxas theme in the background is what got me hooked into the franchise.

stories.author: @FirebrandXVI
stories.text:
Sora: I don't get it. Why's everyone been calling me Roxas?

Riku: Because, Sora... Roxas is your Nobody.

Sora: My... Nobody?! But that's crazy! I never turned into a Heart- Oh, right.

Kairi: It was when you came to rescue me. Remember?

_[Sora nods, remembering how he did save Kairi by releasing her heart that was dormant within Sora's.]_

Riku: Xemnas was the one who found Roxas. He could use the Keyblade because he was your Nobody. That's why Xemnas brought him into the Organization, but Roxas betrayed them. After that I fought him because I thought it would help wake you up. I lost. But the next time we met, I knew I was the stronger one.

_[Flashback to Roxas vs Riku]_

_[Riku tosses Roxas' Oblivion right beside him.]_

_[Roxas, still conscious, picks up Oblivion and swings at Riku, missing his strike. Riku then follows up with a Dark Aura blast and Roxas destroys it with ease, missing his second attack.]_

Roxas: Why won't you quit?!

_[Riku catches on that Roxas is trying to impersonate Sora seeing as he is his Nobody.]_

Riku: Come on, Sora. I thought you were stronger than that.

Roxas: Huh? Get real. Look which one of us is winning.

_[Roxas notices that what he just said sounds exactly like something Sora would say.]_

Riku: So it's true. You really ARE his Nobody. Guess DiZ was right after all.

_[Roxas starts to get angry as he's heard enough about Sora.]_

Roxas: What are you talking about?! I am me. Nobody else!!!

_[Roxas charges at Riku with both Oathkeeper and Oblivion at the ready, missing his first attack but connecting with his secondary strike, staggering Riku.]_

Roxas: How many times do I hafta beat you?

Riku: All right. You've left me with no other choice.

Roxas: What?

Riku: I have to release the darkness in my heart... the dark power that I've been holding back.

_[Riku takes off his blindfold knowing if he has to win the battle at the cost of losing himself to the darkness, he would rather have that fate than perish at the hands of a Nobody.]_

Riku: Even... if it changes me forever.

_[Riku begins to turn to the darkness and changes to Ansem, the same look he had when Sora first faced against him.]_

_[Ansem's Guardian grabs Roxas and starts to strangle the life out of him.]_

Ansem: I have accepted it.

Roxas: Accepted what?

Ansem: The darkness.

_[Roxas' last breath begins to fade as Ansem's Guardian rests him down. DiZ appears behind Ansem and he quickly puts up his hood.]_

Ansem: DiZ, he could feel Sora.

DiZ: Oh, he told you how he felt, did he? Ridiculous. A Nobody cannot feel anything.

Ansem: If he had met Sora, things might have been different.

_[Flashback to present day Sora and Riku]_

Riku: Maybe I didn't need to fight him after all. I think he left the Organization because... he really wanted to meet you.

Sora: Roxas... I wish I could meet him too.

_[Riku points at Sora's heart telling him silently that he doesn't need to meet him; his heart is asleep inside of Sora's. Sora points at his own heart wondering if Riku's right, and he nods in confirmation.]_

Kairi: Come on, you two. Let's go.

stories.text:
Roxas: Axel... Who am I, really?

Axel: *says nothing*

Roxas: I'm special like Xion, I know that. But the Organization wanted me out of the picture. Am I right?

Axel: Yeah... They did.

Roxas: I guess it's 'cause Xion copied my powers, and the Keyblade's powers, and they didn't need me anymore. And Axel, I guess you felt the same way.

Axel: You're wrong there! You'll always be... my best friend.

Roxas: Best friends are supposed to be honest with each other! Who am I, Axel? Xemnas says me and Xion are connected through Sora. I don't even know a Sora! Am I a puppet like Xion!?

Axel: You're different from Xion.

Roxas: Then why d-

Axel: Finding out the truth doesn't always work out for the best!

Roxas: What makes you so sure about that!? I have the right to know the truth! How did I even get here!? Why am I so special!? Where did I learn how to use the Keyblade!? I hardly know who I am! What is so wrong with wanting some answers!?!?!?

Axel: You've just gotta trust me, Roxas.

Axel: Roxas...

Roxas: Somebody knows where I came from. If I can't get answers here, I'll get them from somewhere else. That'll be the person... I trust...

Best argument I've ever listened to in a while.

stories.author: @keybladegames_real
stories.text:
I'll never forget this. Growing up I could NEVER beat demyx. I would just start the game over on another save. Years and I never got to see what it was like after that. But one day I was getting angry again, sick of losing. I messed with abilities trying to give them something to help them survive or do damage cause donald and goofy are useless in kingdom hearts 2 compared to one when their damage actually made a difference in boss fights. I was trying to find something that'd help, just experimenting and one day I found goofy's knocksmash. Seeing it was a team ability I decided to try it. This was the ps2 version so its not nerfed as heavily as it is in the finished version we have now. When I fought demyx and destroyed all his water clones I IMMEDIATELY used knocksmash and I was amazed by the damage, once I shot goofy as a rocket Demyx lost CHUNKS of health and died! It was the fasted boss fight I ever had. I was overjoyed. It took so many years and I finally beat him. So everything beyond that boss encounter was new to me. I was shocked when goofy supposedly died. Seeing Mickey throw his jacket off, summoning his keyblade backwards, I was losing it. I remember running around the house to every family member "Goofy died!" 

It felt good to finally see the game beyond that part. Sad thing is everything else was easy for me. Demyx was the only time I really struggled. But now? I dont struggle. My skills as a gamer got better with age. Now I dont rely on brute strength. I actually use strategy and take my time. Now Demyx is nothing. Hard to believe I struggled so much.

stories.author: @darkmage07070777
stories.text:
The 1K heartless battle was THE moment in KH2 for me. The very first triangle for me was the "Superman dive bomb" attack whatever it's called, and EVERY SINGLE TIME it ended, there was another dive bomb triangle waiting for me to fit it. For 990 enemies, I watch Sora fly up into the air and come crashing down in their midst, like a bird of prey attacking a field of rodents.

And as it happened, I thought about back in KH1 where this same kid was getting his butt beat by three of his friends with play swords. And at that moment, I realized that I had done this. That I had turned Sora the wimp into Sora the demi-god. And this was THE moment that the game started making *ME* feel like a complete badass.

I recall that I started standing on my chair in excitement. Amazing game. Can't wait until KH3 finally comes out.

Man, I remember being so intimidated by the final boss, seeing all those green squares indicating the length of the health bar lol, especially when Xemnas turned into the flying dragon thing and sucked the entire world so you're left fighting a huge monster in a black void. Alone. Just you and Riku fighting a monster that seemed bigger than existence itself. To little me playing the game, it felt encompassing and huge. Truely felt like the end of all worlds. I still remember the daunting feeling I had as a kid, the megalophobia and cosmophobia I felt.  Probably one of the best final boss fights I played because it truly felt "final", y'know? the end to this long journey you've been on and it all comes down to this fight. And ofc it's all brought together by this incredible piece of music.
 
I also love how the dragon monster thing he turned to was made from the white castle in the World that Never Was. I remember being so fascinated as I jumped around the monster and recognized parts of the castle and buildings that I've come across before.

I've seen a video of the final boss fight in KH3, and honestly, I don't think it measures up to the feelings the KH2 final boss fight manages to evoke. Incredible stuff.

stories.author: @mysteriousfigure5996
stories.text:
This game is so special to me. Everytime I boot up KH2, my late brother was always watching me play, like he was my only audience behind me while playing KH2. Thanks to this game our bond became so much stronger. Not until he passed away few years ago, his death hit me hard to the point I lost interest in this series. I tried avoiding things that made me remember him, including avoiding playing KH because it reminds me of him. Because everytime I remember that he's gone and he will never be my audience again while playing KH, I feel so depressed. 

Until KH4 was announced, I was so happy and excited for the upcoming game! My love for this series came back eventually. The more I avoid things that makes me remember him, the more it comes back at me naturally. I feel like my brother's spirit still lingers in me and still guides me wherever I go. The memories we had with this game is the one keeps me moving forward. When I heard this song for the first time again I teared up.

stories.author: @Darkfrost815
stories.text:
I once wondered if I would ever find someone in this world to spend the rest of my life with. Often times I came to the conclusion that I was going to die alone, and I had become alright with that. This song helped me stay calm in very difficult times, and it saved me in many ways. My childhood with this song in it is one of the greatest things I could have ever dreamed of.

Then, 2 and a half years ago, I met my wife. Since the day I met her, my life changed. She has been the best thing to have ever happen to me, and I can finally say I've found my soulmate. Listening to this song has me in tears, because of the overwhelming amount of joy she has brought into my life. I will always love her, and my life will always be better just because she is in it.

Alejandra, I love you with every fiber of my being. Thank you for making my life perfect with just your presence.

stories.author: @caspenknight7464
stories.text:
Kingdom hearts holds a special place in my childhood.
Not only was it a game i spent hours on alone. It was a bounding moment between my siblings and me. I spent a lot of time asking my older brother for help on KH1, especially in Alice's world.
After a while i struggled my way to that Malificent Dragon.
I didn't want to ask for help this time, I was determined. 
I was also on a time limit because my brother was going on deployment soon into the Navy.
In was fighting her while he was getting ready desperately trying to win in time. I had to pause and say good bye to him. I beat her shortly after he left. My brother and I just aren't as close anymore, and i just miss those days.

Kingdom Hearts 2 is where i really bonded with my older sister. I remember helping her with the more skill based challenges, while she helped me with figuring out what to do next. We spent a lot of time together, but in more recent years we didn't talk anymore. I don't know if it was due to mental illness or not, but she thinks everything i do is to spite her. While I really do love my sister and want what is best for her. I don't know how to have her in my life in a positive way, and I don't have the tools to help her. Even still I've tried, and only done more damage to our relationship. I just miss my sister.




Sorry I had nowhere else to dump this.

stories.author: @TayumiUzumaki

So much has happened since she passed and I remember so little about my childhood that I have no idea what she'd even think of me, if she'd be proud of me, etc. Gaming and music were hobbies that she shared with me, and I'm grasping at everything I can to honor her memory for her birthday. And now the tears just won't stop.

stories.author: @juliuskresnik198
stories.text:
It's odd, to be filled with such Nostalgia so early in life. You hear so often as you grow up of how it'll feel, traces of experience, muddled with time and yet fondly remembered nonetheless. 

The melancholy, I didn't expect it tonight.

But, I have so much more life to live. I'm only 22. Recently diagnosed and medicated for a disorder I'd only heard about a year ago. Things make sense now, I feel in control like never before.

And yet, I look back here, this music thawing my disjointed memories and reminding me of the person I was. I see that kid, lost and scared, stumbling about in the dark on his own despite knowing deep down something was wrong. 

He didn't give up. It came close a few times, it really did but at every opportunity, he chose to be better. To be that stubborn little bastard he'd seen on TV and Video Games.

And now, I lay here at night, turning to the next chapter.

I'm learning to drive again, learning to relax, got a new job and I've even got a tentative plan for the future, even if it means starting over again. I'm still that kid but I wouldn't be where I am without the little guy who found peace in this Title Screen, in this game.

The past fills me with a soft sorrow and a warm peace in equal measure, and yet the future calls out to me, the future that little kid had always wanted. I'll take it in both hands and make him proud. I'll add to this collection of disjointed memories. I'll add the laughter, joy, love, excitement, pain, peace and perseverance of a lifetime as the man I've always wanted to be.

I still remember the exact moment I bought this game. It was a used copy in a GameStop and I had never heard of the game before, but the cover and pictures looked really cool to me. Turns out that was the day that I bought my favourite game of all time.
Played through it so many times and often left the main menu open just to listen to this.
The amount of nostalgia I feel when hearing this nowadays is honestly overwhelming and makes me tear up instantly. I wish I could go back to this exact moment of my life and relive all of it for the first time again. I miss waking up in the morning and not having to worry about anything. It truly was the simplest and best time of my life. Thank you to everyone in Square Enix for creating this wonderful game and Yoko Shimomura for composing the most beautiful piece of music. Nothing will ever top this for me.

stories.author: @marcomillan3749
stories.text:
Dear Kingdom Hearts,

I'm writing to express my deepest gratitude for everything you've done for me. When I was a kid, I was bullied and felt like I didn't have any friends. But then I discovered your game, and everything changed.

Through your story and characters, I learned about the power of friendship and the importance of believing in myself. I felt like I was part of something bigger than myself, and that gave me the strength to keep going.

I can't even imagine where I would be today if I hadn't found you. You showed me that no matter how dark things may seem, there's always hope. You gave me a reason to believe in myself and the people around me.

So thank you, from the bottom of my heart. Thank you for saving my life and showing me the true power of friendship.

Sincerely,

Me ❤

stories.author: @CherishedJoysASMR
stories.text:
This game was my escape daydream 24/7, even when not playing. It literally saved my child and teenage self, along with my only friend. Countless nights falling asleep crying, with this song being my lullaby and a hope for better days coming. 
I'm turning 27 this year. Being suicidal, never thought back then I would make it so far. I wanted to unalive myself while listening to this, to finally find peace and be free. 
Now here I am, having not played any of the games for years, as an adult, listening to this. Echoing of times long gone.. I'm crying again.. But it feels cathartic now. All my selves are crying, but the little ones are not alone and scared anymore. 

Dearly beloved indeed. Thank you Yoko Shimomura 🤍

"A scattered dream that's like a far-off memory... a far-off memory that's like a scattered dream... i want to line the pieces up... yours and mine."

stories.text:
"A scattered dream that's like a far off memory. A far off memory that's like a scattered dream. I want to line the pieces up- Yours and mine." The older I get, the more Sora's line resonates with me. 

No matter what point I'm at in life, Dearly Beloved will always be my sanctuary. I filled up an entire memory card of saves for KH2, constantly overwriting old saves to keep playing. it brings me back to that time, where fun didn't have to be supplemented with reason, where the next day was exciting, where being was enough. I don't know if I can ever truly go back to that, but it's something I'm gonna keep striving for, along with all the dreams I had back then and the ones I make now, even if they're impossible or won't go exactly the way I want. Just knowing I tried is enough. It never stopped Sora, Roxas, Riku, or anyone else I looked up to so highly, so why should I stop? This song reminds me of that. It reminds me I have purpose, that I am enough, that even after all this time, how much I've changed, and all the crap I've gone through, I am me.

stories.author: @ScottHamrick01
stories.text: This theme perfectly describes Roxas’ life: Pain. He was brought into this world with nothing to his name, had no idea who he was and when he starts to make friends fighting heartless and hanging out after work to eat Sea Salt Ice Cream. But as we see that Roxas was just a means to an end by Organization XIII, to gather more hearts for Kingdom Hearts, Axel keeping secrets from Roxas and Xion having to fight Roxas so that Sora can wake up and then her existence being forgotten by everyone and taking his anger out on Sora, with the latter having no context or understanding of why Roxas would despise Sora leading to their big fight ending him. This is a major reason why Roxas’ life was always so devastating, he wasn’t allowed to be his own person, have a life to call his own and just a means to an end by the very people he worked for, being manipulated emotionally and mentally making his ‘death’ all the more heartbreaking. But it’s this tragedy that makes Roxas a beloved yet tragic character, a fan favorite if you will. Every time Roxas makes an appearance no matter how brief or unimportant it is people cheer for him and get upset when he disappears back into Sora’s heart, specifically in Dream Drop Distance when Sora tells Roxas that they are not the same and that he deserves to exist just as much as Sora does. And learning everything he has had to endure and what Sora took away from him Sora is understandably horrified of what happened to him and swears to bring him back, which we see in Kingdom Hearts III, after the concept of vessels is introduced not only fighting alongside Axel and Xion but Sora as well. Roxas saying he needed Sora’s help to return says that he accepted his fate long ago and has no reason to hate him with a remix of Roxas’ theme playing upon being revealed, every fan from across the world cried tears of joy cheering for his big comeback is a testament to who Roxas is and what he means to the fans

_[Xion looks sad to see Axel in front of the mansion in Twilight Town]_

Xion: Axel...

stories.author: @tusk8230
stories.text: Everybody is dishing out a lot of appreciation for the character, today I'm going to dish out appreciation for the fight. It's a wonderful duel, for me it's an example of a battle where I feel like every loss is my own fault. Each of us attacks have good telegraphs and are simple to dodge if you have good timing, good rhythm, and you know the signs. And due to the way that his attacks come out, there are many ways to react to them, and therefore many more ways to counter them. As an example, I block the first attack at the beginning of the fight and then when he does the jumping slash instead of blocking it I roll to the side and then thrust forwards from the side to get him in a combo. The way that this battle was designed so that there were so many different approaches, so that the battle relied equally on good reading and split second reactions makes this a battle that I shall never forget.

Giving nobodies a heart over time as stated in Dream Drop Distance, just removes the actual impact of the characters.

heres a graph if that last bit was confusing:

                        heartless

                                                                 another nobody(now with a heart)

oh, but now he has a heart, so that was all just a hehehehaw.

stories.text: I knocked on my brother's bedroom door to let him know that supper was ready, no response. So I opened the door, it was pitch black, I couldn't even see the bed. I stepped forward to find the light switch only to realize, there is no step to take. I tried to grab the door frame but missed, and fell into the dark abyss. As I fell, I noticed sparks surround me as my appearance changed before my eyes, my hair turned white, my skin turned dark gray, and my pajamas turned into leather armor, meawhile, my phone fell out of my pocket and started changing as well. After making ground impact, I got up and picked up the device that used to be my phone to examine it. I pushed a button on the side, and it extended into a red and black sniper/scythe hybrid. I pushed the button again for it to retract, then placed it in my inventory and begin the surch for my brother.

stories.text:
The abyss you have fallen into is empty. All you can feel is a familiar emptiness, as if you were in the voids keeping neighbors apart, or say, the very floor beneath your feet had been stolen. A familiar sound comes from somewhere. It's the same one the guitar of December used to play.

It is your seventeenth year on this planet, and your brother will be home from college on Sunday, the day of the festival. And yet, as with every day since that night, you cannot help but feel a sense of desperation, one that has guided you in a terrible direction, one you are unable to stray from. The chains given to you by Fate are unbreakable, and yet, you hope that one day you will break them.

“Freedom is never voluntarily given by the oppressor; it must be demanded by the oppressed.” - C.S. Lewis

Yes, you are certain C.S. Lewis said that. One hundred percent positive.

. . .

You have a feeling it's going to be a long four days.

*_deltarune_*

stories.author: @thegoldenblob69
stories.text:
Something I realized.

So, Kris's family is divorced, their brother's off to college, and their relationship with the Holidays have long since faded - what with Dess missing/dead and all. 

But, then there was the girl.

Susie is new, she moved in some time ago. 

Darkners, are objects, toys, entertainment. Physical toys (cards, board games, etc), Laptops (internet/offline), TV (local, movies, etc), Church is all about community (plus free juice) and so that's another opportunity to connect with people.

'Darkners,' help lightners connect and understand one another. You and your friends get together to do a school project, but end up goofing off on the public library computer instead. Your friends crash out at your/their place and watch TV into the night. You and your friends might simply go to church, even if they arent super religious, just to have a community (and drink fruit juice).

Susie, by being new and not knowing the deep history that runs in the town, is able to rekindle that bond between everyone. Susie is the one bring Kris to places, talking to Noelle when no one else is around, giving a one to one with Ralsei, heck, even giving a damn about berdly one time. 

She is a new friend. If anyone has experienced bouts of loneliness or struggles making friends, having that one person, that single person, just suddenly appear in your life, can make a huge difference. Just someone who gets you, someone who feels for you and is always there. 

For Kris, it might be due to basically being alone for who knows how long. Holidays rarely come over, their dad is practically in rags, their mom is an alcoholic who only sees "her child" and not Kris, and their brother is at college. None of the other kids or other adolescents connect with Kris in any meaningful way. Then there's Susie, who connects with Kris, and is hanging out with them in ways they probably havent done or felt similar to in years.

Noelle's older sister, December, is either missing or dead. Carol is an overworked, harsh, and strict mother. Rudy is in the hospital, possibly on his deathbed. Noelle, for most of her childhood and adolescence, has lacked that older, more mature figure in her life. Rudy jokes too much while Carol, in the rare instances shes actually home and not working, is a total 180 and is way too harsh. Dess more than likely was the grounding figure. She hit Kris with a wiffle bat when they scared Noelle as kids. 

Susie, during the "mouse" seen, very much acted like that mature, and down to earth figure that Noelle has desperately been missing in her life thus far. 


The Legend makes it seem like their life, for both Kris and Noelle, is just the way things are. Kris's parents are divorced, Noelle's older sister, Dess, is gone. Nothing will be the same.

Then, there was the girl. Love finds its way to the girl. Susie warms up to her new friends, realizing this is not going to be like last time. She wont be a bully, she wont just move this time. She'll have friends now. 
Kris isnt going to be just the weird kid, they're not going to be lonely and misunderstood/lack connection forever. They'll have friends. Noelle's older sister, Dess, is still out there. We will find her. Even then, Susie is there for Noelle. Noelle will get stronger, and she will have Susie to help her break out her shell and grow into a better person. Berdly... uh... he'll learn hubris.

On a serious note, given Berdly's behavior in the Library in Chapter 4, I genuinely have high hopes for him. It seems he's on the path to becoming a better person. He acts like a chill and even empathetic dude once he no longer has that smarty know-it-all attitude. 

Still, I believe the main plot of Deltarune thus far is: Making new friends who connect with you and hanging out with them in various ways can help change your fate as a person. Time is always changing.

(I'm not including US, the soul, because thats another can of worms. Love is very much also referring to us gaining more and more control over Susie each chapter in some capacity. I really hope we dont fully possess her like we do with Kris. 

ALSO CAN WE GET OUR VESSEL?!?! (pls)

stories.author: @dtdbkarma9086
stories.text:
It was an age of tragic mistakes. Seven long years. A lot of memories and a rollercoaster of emotions, seemed to pass in the blink of an eye. I look back. I gaze around at the buildings I used to run, jump, play and learn in and around. I look at the tall pine trees, branches swaying gently in the midmorning breeze. I stare longingly out towards the ocean, glistening in the summer sun. 

This was once my home. Now there is nothing here for me but tears, and memories. 

Merely thinking of my friends and family causes tears to well up behind my eyes. How seriously I took life when there was nothing for me to worry about. When I still had people who I could rely on, and who could rely on me. I miss them more than simple words can express. They're gone now, and it's all my fault. And there is nothing I can do to put things right. 

I continue to look out over what was, for most of my life, my entire world. Strange, isn't it? How a place can mean so much to you, yet you can mean so little to it? When people begin to wake up, when they start to go about another lazy December day, when the town begins to come back to life, it will all go on without me. I will not be missed in the slightest. Life will go on. Business as usual.

Enough dwelling. The past is an ideal that can never be reclaimed. We must always look ahead, learning from what has been, but never letting ourselves be controlled by it. I close my eyes and breathe the coastal air deep. The smell of grass fills my nostrils as I about face. The sun beats down on my face. It's going to be a scorcher. My rucksack weighs on me. I bow my head. It finally hits me that to this place, I am gone - dead and buried, and there is not turning back. I take my first step forward. Into the unknown, across the Field of Hopes and Dreams.

edit from post-chapter 5, includes spoilers for weird route up to chapter 5: okay so it's been like 6 years since i've made this comment, and people have been replying to it since then, so i'd like to put in my two cents.

i don't consider weird route "undertale's genocide route" at all. aside from the fact that you only need to freeze all the enemies in a very small part of the game, the idea of weird route -- from what i can tell -- is to fit the idea of "breaking the game" into a compelling narrative about two young characters who have been through something tragic in the past, and haven't been the same since.

and that's the cool thing about toby's writing: the way he uses the mechanics of videogames to tell a story. in undertale, flowey wasn't simply calling undertale a literal game -- his life had become a game at that point, as he was able to turn back time at will, and therefore predict the actions and dialogue of everyone in the underground. his options for what to do and say became limited, because everyone became incredibly predictable, driving him to murder, just to see what would happen. deltarune is much like that -- although with ralsei's "icons" exposition, it seems as if they were to discuss the meta of this world as a game, they also described it as a thing seen in the sub-conscience only in the dark world, continuing to tie gameplay mechanics into the world. 

and that applies to weird route too.

weird route is an exploration of game-breaking through the eyes of kris and noelle, who have both dealt with mental health issues likely since the event asgore alluded to in chapter 5 -- issues that have caused noelle to shrink into a role which she describes as watching herself through glass. to break free of that loop she's been caught in, she must break free of her town (the game) itself -- spread wings and fly somewhere no one has ever gone before.

and kris... well, i'll be honest, i have a lot of thoughts about kris's perspective that very much deter from the norm of what most perceive of them, so i won't get into that. all i will say is that, while a large part of them doesn't want this -- hates themself for it, especially the parts of them that _do_ want this -- they're trapped in a doomed prophecy, and although we don't yet know what the end of said prophecy is at this point, it's something that clearly disturbs kris based on the flavour text if you look at the shadow crystal in the final prophecy room ("You held the crystal up to your eye. For some strange reason... The prophecy's text does not warp in the crystal's lens. You shook the crystal... However, nothing changed."). perhaps they see the route noelle suggests as a way to escape such a fate, and that's why they encourage her forward -- hesitating at first, thus the option to say "stop", but eventually pushing forward, with the option to "stop" fading from their mind.

basically, my thoughts have seriously changed since i wrote this back when chapter 1 first came out. i think back then i considered deltarune as undertale 2, but it's its own story, with its own rich narrative, and i am thrilled by the prospects of where weird route could take us.

So, let me get this straight.
Susie hates being lied to and deceived. This isn't the first time it's happened, she's quick to assume things without thinking and refuses to hear people out, thinking they're all out to screw her over.
Her two best friends, Kris and Ralsei, are both the biggest goddamn liars we've met so far. Kris is pulling a triple-agent trying to make all sides happy, and Ralsei knows both about us puppeteering Kris and the prophecy, and refused to tell anyone about it for pretty weak reasons. 
Susie has absolutely zero clue about almost all of this. She didn't stop to think about what _else_ Ralsei is lying about, so she's in the dark about it, and Kris has done a very good job of hiding our interloper status overall between all their meddling.
Conclusion, it's virtually inevitable that this is all gonna come to a head in a future chapter, maybe 6 or somewhere 'round there, where she finds out it's all made up. She refuses to listen to either of them telling her that it's more complicated than that, she doesn't care. She's been lied to, and she hates people who don't tell the whole story, so therefore she hates Kris and Ralsei. Simple as that.

stories.author: @LoyTheClown
stories.text: The internal struggle of a girl with a broken life having to make herself kill her effectively best friend and only true friend at the time, her rough-n-tough ruse falling. The song is full of power and strength, yet unutilized to its fullest. immense power courses from the song, but it can't stick. the guitar's long notes are strong but, they fall off of that stength, like failing to fully commit. Her rage is conflicted. she DESPISES how she was betrayed. but she can't fully see herself commiting to what she's doing. it's her character breaking down. the start of the song represents her facade at the start of the chapter. Closed off, muffled, heard, but never allowing anyone to enter that bubble to hear the TRUTH. the song starts strong and concrete, but it starts to drift and distort before the beat drops. This is when she gets through the chapter to lancer, letting her guard down for someone who just accepted her, and looked past all the attempts to deter her. then, the beat slows, being when lancer runs from the fun gang after the near the castle. then, after exiting the cell, she sees lancer, and realizes what happened, the music starting back up, the rage, the betrayal, everything coming in. over time the hits continue, and then comes 0:53 in the song. This is when she starts to break. She TRIES to commit to ruining the traitor. She TRIES to prove she's strong enough to take out something that'd humiliate her. trick her like this. but each riff doesnt stick to its starting intensity, nor does it increase. it falls off and drops. Her commitment to this slips. Her emotions take over the facade, fighting the tide of her outburst at lancer. she doesn't want this. the music hits its most dramatic and most significant peak here, being the culmination of everything, when she either kills lancer or lets the facade finally not control her any longer. yes i just wrote an essay over a less than 2 minute long song from 7 years ago.

stories.author: @uboa8060
stories.text:
This might be the best cover of The World Revolving I've heard.

Admittedly, in recent years, I've grown a lot more cynical in my opinion about "nerdcore" VGM lyrical covers because sometimes they get very amateurish and I find myself nitpicking and overanalyzing every time I listen to a given cover. I only want to do that on my first or second listen of anything, I want every subsequent listen to make me slip further and further away from thinking about the lyrics and quality and further into just vibing, and this cover flawlessly achieved that in just two listens. After a couple listens, it'll probably overtake Man on the Internet's cover as my favorite, really. 

I don't want to make it sound like a competition, but if it was, you're easily a front runner for over all quality and lyricism with VGM covers I listen to. I remember listening to your Black Knife cover a bunch, and while the MOTI cover became my personal favorite when it came out, I'm probably gonna go listen to your's again right now, lol.

stories.author: @June_girl8
stories.text:
Okay, speculating on some of the lyrics that stuck out to me: 

“It’s so much fun to watch you run around
And ring around the rose
Around the rows and rows of common folk
The court before the throne
I’m freer than a God but 
never my own…”

First off, the wordplay here is really satisfying and like- I love the vaguest hint that even he feels the stifling nature of the prophecy through his insanity- that the only reason he’s been granted his “little freedom” is because- well whatever happened back then with gaster/friend/the shadow crystal- his freedom is not his own- but he can still revel in it until his world inevitably ends- or whatever the final prophecy is. 

“I’m helpless, oh what a delight!” - also this defnitely supports that view- what Jevils “freedom” is is intentionally vague, but perhaps it’s something to do with how he found out about the “system layer” I suppose I’ll call it, (though perhaps he saw deeper than that?)  and in that crushing existential realization, he deluded himself into thinking that that knowledge gives him more room to move around in his role in the prophecy- or even like, the fact that he’s “fine” in that knowledge is the freedom that nobody else has.

“Light, light is never enough 
Heaven is shining bright”

these automatically sound oddly Spamton sounding- but then like- it immediately precedes

“But Hell can call your bluff
Let's rejoice in frenzy”

So it feels to me like he’s calling out those like Spamton or actually probably the fun gang for following the prophecy/gaster/heaven, and he’s like taunting them here

But theeennn he references hell when he does so- which like- yeah Jevil is def connected to hell/friend/depths - which is feeding into my theory that FRIEND has smth to do with the shadow crystals - like actually gave them out or something. 

Even now I feel like this is just surface level stuff… but there’s just not the most stuff for jevil… ughhh he’ll come back right - the bajillion world revolving references in chapter 5 mean something right Toby? Right??? 

Anyways, this was so good! I’m consistently so blown away by your vocals :3
