stories.author: @imnightmare101
stories.text:
The Sans fight is quite possibly my favorite boss fight in not only Undertale, but all of gaming. And the reason why goes far beyond just the actual gameplay of the fight itself, even if I do find said fight and difficulty to be enjoyable gameplay wise.
No, the real reason is because of everything this fight represents. There's layers and layers I could go into, so much so that I could never possibly hope to get all my thoughts and praise on it out in a single Youtube comment, but I'll try my best. Something I like about it, which might sound counterproductive, is how anticlimatic it feels compared to the True Pacifist final boss, Asriel Dreemurr.

The fight with Asriel is far more like your traditional video game RPG final boss. After all, it is often joked about that you go from fighting small creatures to fighting gods or godlike entities in the end, and Undertale is no different. But the thing that makes Undertale so special to me, is that Undertale is unlike your usual RPG game. Sure, you do fight Asriel at the end of the Pacifist route, the game's 'intended' ending, but much like Sans, there's more than meets the eye to this game. Because personally, I think the TRUE ending to the game is this. Not every player goes onto play the genocide route, and you're completely valid in choosing not to do so, but in my opinion? You're missing what sets Undertale apart from so many other games.

So many people simplify the genocide route's message to simply be 'killing is bad.' That's not the point, and that was never the point. I personally believe the real aim of the genocide run was to explore how people interact with and 'complete' games. After finishing a pacifist run, the player is faced with a conundrum. Do they leave the game forever, content with the pacifist ending? Or will they let their curiosity get the best of them and see what else the game has to offer? This is all too similar to what Flowey is faced with before Frisk falls into the underground, and what does he end up doing? He eventually gives into his boredom, and begins to kill just to see what will happen. 

When the player first meets Flowey and perhaps falls for his trick, they're likely to see Flowey as an irredeemable monster. It's only when they learn about his backstory on the genocide route they find that Flowey has actually been a 'mirror' of us, the player, the entire time. And, of course, this is mere moments before the player fights Sans for the very first time.
Something I find interesting about Sans, is how in a sense, he's somewhat 'disjointed' from the rest of the main characters you meet throughout the game. Each of the other main characters are clear with their intentions and are tied to the game's story. Toriel and Asgore are (formally in Toriel's case) the rulers of the underground, Papyrus wants to be in the royal guard, Undyne leads the royal guard, you get the idea.

Sans? The only real link he has to the story, is simply being the brother of Papyrus. He's not like Papyrus who actively pushes the story along, such as when he encourages you to befriend Undyne or tells you to meet up with the other monsters before the Asriel fight, which leads to their souls being absorbed. Sans... is just there. And through several clues in the game that I don't enough text to elaborate on right now, it's implied he comes from another world. 

Sans, and by extension his fight, stand out among all the other battles in the game. For example, with the fight against Asriel Dreemurr? That fight is a culmination of the game's story, Asriel and Chara's deaths eventually leading to Asriel being reborn as Flowey and then receiving godlike powers, hoping that he can see 'Chara' again. That is clearly set in the world of Undertale.
Sans's fight? It has practicially nothing to do with the story of the game. Sans has nothing to do with Asriel or Chara, or the war that sealed monsterkind away underground. It's about YOU. It's about everyone that has played a game to completion before. It represents the drive to keep persisting with something, to see everything something has to offer, until there's nothing left.

'no matter what, you'll just keep going. not out of any desire for good or evil... but just because you think you can.
 and because you "can"...
... you "have to.''

Sans fighting you is about so much more than a wacky species of 'monsters' being trapped in a mountain. Sans isn't just fighting for his own world... in a sense, he's fighting for every world. Every other world that's at risk of you picking it apart, and then discarding it just as you've had enough of it. Don't believe me? What happens after you kill Sans?
'don't say i didn't warn you.'
Sans walks off screen and fades to dust. You walk into Asgore's room and Flowey lands the final blow on him. Flowey then begs for you not to kill him, his face and voice even contorting to match that of Asriel's. Only to die a violent death, being attacked until there's nothing left of him. I believe that represents the death of the illusion of the game's narrative, one that had already been thrown off course by you beginning the genocide route in the first place. Flowey's death was the final nail in the coffin, as afterwards Chara speaks directly to you.

'Let us erase this pointless world, and move on to the next.'

Like I said, by 'moving on to the next', Chara isn't setting up a sequel to Undertale or anything where you go on a killing rampage. Chara is talking about the other games you've played, the other 'worlds' you've torn asunder trying to squeeze it for all of its worth until you dispose of it. Which is why Sans says this:

'you'll keep consuming timelines over and over, until... well. someday...
you gotta learn when to QUIT.'

Sans isn't fighting only to avenge the people he loves, although make no mistake, he's definitely affected by that as well. That's why I said there's layers. You can look at the fight from both a meta perspective, and a non meta perspective (which is what most of the fandom seems to have done.) But it's the fact that both of these factors work in tandem that makes the fight so perfect in my eyes. I really would love to talk more about it, but I'm still only scratching the surface of everything this fight represents.

stories.author: @Goji-h1g
stories.text: “Hi. Seems as if everyone is perfectly happy. Monsters have returned to the surface. Peace and prosperity will rule across the land. Take a deep breath. There's nothing left to worry about. ... Well. There is one thing. One last threat. One being with the power to erase EVERYTHING... everything everyone's worked so hard for. ... You know who I'm talking about, don't you? That's right. I'm talking about YOU. YOU still have the power to reset everything. Toriel, Sans, Asgore, Alphys, Papyrus, Undyne... if you so choose... everyone will be ripped from this timeline... and sent back before all of this ever happened. Nobody will remember anything. You'll be able to do whatever you want. ... That power. I know that power. That's the power you were fighting to stop, wasn't it? The power that I wanted to use. But now, the idea of resetting everything... I... I don't think I could do it all again. Not after that. ... So, please. Just let them go. Let Frisk be happy. Let Frisk live their life. ... But. If I can't change your mind. If you DO end up erasing everything... ... You have to erase my memories, too. ... I'm sorry. You've probably heard this a hundred times already, haven't you...? ... Well, that's all. See you later... Chara.”

Honestly really didn't like 10-2 as a game.

The not true new game+, the way they structured the game; I only ever did one play through because I didnt realize the first time through that doing the essential missions locked you out of the early stages of other side quests.


The semi bastardization of one of my favorite FF mechanics, namely job/job change system.

The thinly veiled charlies angles rip off theming.

Lastly, while I did not like how 10 originally ended, it was by no means, a bad ending, just not the one I wanted, there are many times I've felt this way in the past, just because the ending was not the one I wanted does not mean the ending was bad, but 10-2 retconned the ending and with some half hearted bullshit too.

Anyways all this was to say that, this song however, even to date haunts me... brings back such a strong sense of nostalgia and longing for the past and times long gone, for things before they changed and things I will never regain... this and 1000's words were the only parts of this game I found redeemable.

Replayed this game this past month for the first time since it released in the States. Actually blown away by how well it has aged. There's some cringe in there, but if you can get through it, it represents the apex of the ATB system in FF and arguably the best of the job system as well, rolled into one. A campy romp through old stomping grounds culminating in an emotional ending, and it's kicked off by the best track the game has to offer right up front on the menu. Didn't hurt that it was my first time being exposed to everything the International release added.

These fantasy worlds we experienced when we were children really did become a part of us. Something magical about coming home for awhile.

stories.author: @deaththeclover
stories.text:
I fell in love with this theme when I heard it. It gives off *SOO* much story, like that feeling of: peace has finally come at last. 

Everyone is living happily! Wakka and Lulu are legendary guardians watching over the town and their newborn baby, stepping into parenting together. The Besaid Aurochs are still doing what they do best, practicing for the next blitz season ready for whatever challenges await them. Now they are probably known as the best team all throughout Spira.

But under all the happiness of this song, there’s a tinge of something missing, a burning feeling of sadness. For many people, its the sadness of Tidus not being around to enjoy the peace he helped bring to Spira. But for me it’s the feeling of *NEVER* being able to experience the story and the world SE sprung to life for the first time ever again. That alone just breaks my heart...

stories.author: @OpenOceanOnly
stories.text: The original Besaid theme is one of my favorite instrumental tracks of all time. I absolutely hate the "re-master" version, but I forgot how good the FFX-2 version is. It seems to be an "answer" to the original: the FFX version has a feeling of being in awe of the natural beauty around you while also having the repeating, dissident low tone to remind you of the impending doom that is Sin. This version has a feeling of bittersweet memories mixed with the comfort of home, since it is the place Yuna can most call home. People think Nobuo Uematsu is the be-all-end-all of Final Fantasy music, but people forget that two other composers worked with him for FFX (one of whom made the original Besaid track) and he had no involvement with the series after that.

stories.author: @ahorseofficial
stories.text: I've never been into playing video games so much, but I loved to watch my brother play them when I was young. Back then my mother was still alive, my family was all so close. It was warm, carefree. Since then many things had happened and my brother and I grew apart. A decade plus some years later, I found this song again. I have no musical talent, but I was determined to learn this song at least partially on the piano. When I came home from school one day my mother had coincidentally purchased a really old piano and placed it in the living room. The next morning as my brother was still sleeping, I focused and played this song to the best of my lackluster ability. My brother wakes up and barrels down the hallway trying to figure out the song that I was playing was and why he remembers it so well. After a few guesses he says "Kingdom Hearts?" I like to think ever since that moment we have been slowly reforming our bond. We are nothing alike and agree on almost nothing as adults, but at least that one moment will stay with me forever.

stories.author: @internetphenomenon734
stories.text:
I'm 33 years old. I lived in a big house with a few acres of woods behind it. I have 4 siblings - one is my older brother by two years, another my younger by two years. The three of us, and occasionally my FOURTH brother, would play together in the woods when we were kids. I loved those woods. We would pretend all the standard fare for 00's kids - Pokemon, Lord of the Rings, Star Wars, even some Digimon. We had wild imaginations, and our adventures always had to do with fighting evil creatures, or catching Pokemon, if that was the flavor of the day. I was homeschooled, so I didn't have to deal with public school and its pressures.

Kingdom Hearts was a favorite of mine, even though I hardly ever played. I watched older bro play it and let my mind create the adventure. It was fun watching him play it, we had pretty much grown out of pretending. When I heard Dearly Beloved for the first time, I was at the same stage as Sora. I was on an idyllic island with only a few of my closest friends, where nothing much happened. But I could feel it - I was ready to go. The outside world was beckoning, with all its adventures, and I had to answer.

Of course I left the island, and of course it was painful. Growing always is. But I will never forget those memories - excitement and safety, the feeling that there in those woods, with my friends, I had everything I needed. This song reminds me of that safety, and of the bittersweet voyage towards Purpose that all of us must take.

stories.author: @Tweekitus
stories.text:
Fuck me... I bought this game without knowing exactly what I was getting into. 22 years later, I can't help but think back to the time when I first dipped my toes into KH1. It was so captivating, and I remember crying like a baby at the ending when Kairi and Sora were separated.

This series will genuinely go down in history. It can be argued that it is genuine emotional porn, but at least we got characters who felt real. Sora knows he's not the smartest, but he trusts in his friends and realizes that having people to back him up makes him stronger. Riku lost his way, but he realized how wrong he was and fought tooth and fucking nail to make it right, eventually accepting that he could use the parts of him that he disliked to help do good.

Yes, you have to suspend your disbelief a bit and accept the fact that the storytelling tends to lean toward "if it sounds/feels good, it works," but I will never in my life regret the story that I got to experience. And KH1 began it all with a little boy who just wanted to see what the greater world was really like.

stories.text: Its already been four years since I first experienced this gem of a series, and yet somehow, this song is just as nostalgic to me as it was when I first heard it. No matter the occasion, my mood, how long I listen to it, etc., it never fails to remind me of times long gone, never failing to make me weep. There's something about this melody that resonates so strongly with the human soul that it feels like its always been a part of it. This song is your family, your parent's cooking, your closest friends, your pets, your childhood home, your first kiss, your high school graduation, that one memory that is so unbelievably inconsequential but you never fail to forget, and countless more experiences put into sound all at once. Like the waves of the ocean, memories wash over you until you are enveloped by the sea of your soul. A true dive to the heart.

stories.author: @randymarshislorde
stories.text:
For those like me who experienced this game on or near it's release date... You guys remember? Remember how it seemed to drag your mind into a state where you were convinced you may have been dreaming during your first time going through the dive to the heart and doing the intro sequence? Then you get into the initial quests on the island, you do the race, you collect supplies, you go swimming all over the beachfront on both sides, convinced there is some kind of secret to discover? Remember how you got so comfortable that it approached boring?

I (in my very young mind) was actually convinced that we'd go out on that raft and run into the Disney characters we were promised on some small-medium islands that were located around the ocean. Tbh I anticipated a fairly mild adventure. Then things started to get weird, ansem in the cave was the first sign that things werent gonna go how I expected, then waking up to the storm, hearing this theme, meeting Darkside... It was crazy. 

Then to my complete shock, we hit traverse town. To this day that town is among my top 5 list of fictional places I'd like to live in if I one day woke up sucked into a fictional world. Man the design of that place.. such wonderful nostalgic memories.

stories.author: @GamerDude5432
stories.text: What i feel when i hear this song is Longing. I long for the days when i was young, for when i visited my older cousin playing together and like Sora and Riku, the days before the family drama, before the school trauma, the days where i was blisfully unawear of my crippling loneliness, the days where i could hang out with my best friend without realizing that he began to distance himself from me. I still have dreams about it all, my Classmates, my best friend, my cousin, but i know they don’t care, none of them do. They’ve never cared enough to know how i was doing, to ask me if i wanted to hang out with them, to try and contact me again even after so long. Sometimes i think about that scene, the one where Sora flies through the darkness, and reaching the light of his heart, Kairi, Riku, Donald, and Goofy all being that light, the ones who keep him going, and always bring him back from the darkness, and i just can’t help but feel jelous of it. It’s stupid, he’s a fictional character, but he still has so much, his heart is always with his friends, and theirs are all with him aswell, but i’ve never had that, i’ve never had someone fill that void i’ve had in my heart since i was 13. Back then, i was young and naive, unawear of it even being there, but now i very much do. And maybe one day i’ll finally find it, that light i keep reaching out to, maybe a friend, maybe a brother, maybe a Partner or even a Lover, and maybe when i do, these dreams will finally end. But i don’t have my hopes up, because i’m already a lost cause. I hate this feeling.

stories.text:
I have so many memories of this song. The first was my first time hearing the song. I already knew that I was going to Hollow Bastion and that it was late game, but I had no idea about this track. I immediately though "Oh shit, we're approaching end game! This song is epic!" Before I learned about Youtube, I went through this route repeatedly just to hear this song.

Another memory was when I was flying home from Korea after spending six weeks there. I listened to the entire KH soundtrack to help me get through the flight. I was sitting in the window seat. As this song came on, I opened my window shade to see that it was nighttime outside, and a wonderful view of the moon above the clouds. I'll never forget it.

stories.text: I got to admit this was a cool level in concept yet at the same time as I played through I sort of dreaded it a little bit because of the fact that due to being partially blind with severe optic nerve damage let's just say the dungeon oh man I track myself more times then I wanted to because not only did every way look the same but it was so dark in that area that I would accidentally trigger a switch that I had already triggered which would set me off course and it really sucked and like I said don't even give me started on the library man if only you could carry more than one book at a time especially two of the books are like the same color but the patterns are different just by a small margin. I mean I cannot tell you how many times I have gotten tricked by the bindings of those books and the fact that you can only really hold one at a time kind of sucks too like I mentioned the last time it would have been cool if they gave us a backpack so we could collect everything they needed and one go and just use it up as we go that would have made things a heck of a lot easier instead of all the backtracking and confusion between two different pattern books I mean man and having to use the thunder spell to get one of the books was painful not to mention a lot of the Trinity marks in that game were very hard for me to find due to my vision issues and especially the one where you had to climb like a ladder just to get a book from a shelf that kind of tanked also I mean in concept it was a cool level design but I feel like they really should have thought it through a little bit better I mean of course sure it's the first game but and everything's just an experiment but at the same time I really feel like when they did the remasters they could have improved on that especially I'm surprised that deep jungle made it back in to the game because of them losing the rights to Turner but I'm pretty sure that Turner let them do it due to the fact that if they took that world out the game would practically be incomplete but the back tracking in that area was a tornado in a handbasket and thank gosh I'm not the only one who thinks that. In other words, it seems like a lot of people had the same thought as I did and thank goodness!

It's not the town you grew up in anymore. No, it's just another town that has fallen victim to the ravages of time. Deep down, you knew it was coming, yet you still had to go, still had to see it for yourself. And now you see it, you feel a sense not of sadness, but of peace. stories.author: @deegeayy
stories.text: End of the World’s theme and level design was just so mesmerizing to me as a kid. The theme is practically a reprise of the first song you hear in the game, but fuller. The first view you have is an event horizon of purples and blues amongst a seemingly endless sea of nothing. Then, as you press on, you venture through shards of worlds you thought you saved. Seeing the Hundred Acre Wood here of all places was shocking to 10 year old me. Then, at the *end* of the end, you find yourself back on a fragment of Destiny Islands… the place where it all began. I hadn’t played any other games that went this deep into level design when I was younger. So this easily stands out as one of the best places in gaming. Even if this place wasn’t as impactful as The World That Never Was, it’s still a stellar final world

stories.author: @ahorseofficial
stories.text: I've never been into playing video games so much, but I loved to watch my brother play them when I was young. Back then my mother was still alive, my family was all so close. It was warm, carefree. Since then many things had happened and my brother and I grew apart. A decade plus some years later, I found this song again. I have no musical talent, but I was determined to learn this song at least partially on the piano. When I came home from school one day my mother had coincidentally purchased a really old piano and placed it in the living room. The next morning as my brother was still sleeping, I focused and played this song to the best of my lackluster ability. My brother wakes up and barrels down the hallway trying to figure out the song that I was playing was and why he remembers it so well. After a few guesses he says "Kingdom Hearts?" I like to think ever since that moment we have been slowly reforming our bond. We are nothing alike and agree on almost nothing as adults, but at least that one moment will stay with me forever.

stories.author: @internetphenomenon734
stories.text:
I'm 33 years old. I lived in a big house with a few acres of woods behind it. I have 4 siblings - one is my older brother by two years, another my younger by two years. The three of us, and occasionally my FOURTH brother, would play together in the woods when we were kids. I loved those woods. We would pretend all the standard fare for 00's kids - Pokemon, Lord of the Rings, Star Wars, even some Digimon. We had wild imaginations, and our adventures always had to do with fighting evil creatures, or catching Pokemon, if that was the flavor of the day. I was homeschooled, so I didn't have to deal with public school and its pressures.

Kingdom Hearts was a favorite of mine, even though I hardly ever played. I watched older bro play it and let my mind create the adventure. It was fun watching him play it, we had pretty much grown out of pretending. When I heard Dearly Beloved for the first time, I was at the same stage as Sora. I was on an idyllic island with only a few of my closest friends, where nothing much happened. But I could feel it - I was ready to go. The outside world was beckoning, with all its adventures, and I had to answer.

Of course I left the island, and of course it was painful. Growing always is. But I will never forget those memories - excitement and safety, the feeling that there in those woods, with my friends, I had everything I needed. This song reminds me of that safety, and of the bittersweet voyage towards Purpose that all of us must take.

stories.author: @emy.h64
stories.text:
I'm 12. I'm watching the Kindgom Hearts trailer with awe, my child's eyes amazed by its beauty and the endless possibilities it means to me. I look for the soundtrack, and discover this particular piece. I feel a strong nostalgia for a game I didn't even play, for a time I still belong to. I wonder if I'll play one of this games someday.
I'm 15. Sometimes I stumble upon a trailer, some news about the Kingdom Hearts community. I remember I was fascinated by these games, so I look for the soundtrack. Once again, this piece speaks to me.
I'm 18. I use this music to study. I still feel the nostalgia, but it is now intertwined with a peaceful feeling. I hear Kingdom Hearts III is in development. I'm happy, even though I won't play it. I don't have a PS, and the entirety of the series isn't playable on it anyway.
I'm 21. It's Christmas, and my girlfriend, who owns a PS4, gives me my present. She bought me the entirety of the series in the remastered pack, which was just released. I feel like I could cry, but I smile, a lot.
I'm 21. I press the button. I hear this piece, and I heard it countless time now, but it feels new. The sound of a childhood dream come true. I'm 21, but I'm 12 again, watching the game starts with awe, travelling back to my childhood. To a dearly beloved time.

stories.author: @Tweekitus
stories.text:
Fuck me... I bought this game without knowing exactly what I was getting into. 22 years later, I can't help but think back to the time when I first dipped my toes into KH1. It was so captivating, and I remember crying like a baby at the ending when Kairi and Sora were separated.

This series will genuinely go down in history. It can be argued that it is genuine emotional porn, but at least we got characters who felt real. Sora knows he's not the smartest, but he trusts in his friends and realizes that having people to back him up makes him stronger. Riku lost his way, but he realized how wrong he was and fought tooth and fucking nail to make it right, eventually accepting that he could use the parts of him that he disliked to help do good.

Yes, you have to suspend your disbelief a bit and accept the fact that the storytelling tends to lean toward "if it sounds/feels good, it works," but I will never in my life regret the story that I got to experience. And KH1 began it all with a little boy who just wanted to see what the greater world was really like.

stories.author: @sai6724
stories.text:
I'm here after playing the Re:Mind DLC.

The string instruments just add so much emotion. They express the sentiment of so much hidden pain, grief, unresolved anger, desperation and perhaps something even more underneath, like it wants... needs something to be resolved, but only through battle. Its like a lead up to a huge battle that will someday be fought.

This track is so, so powerful. I'm honestly driven to tears just listening to this. Imagine the hero on a mission to save someone they love while this track plays in the middle of a huuuuge, otherworldly and ethereal city full of mysterious lore and secrets waiting to have all of its doors opened to all who desire to know its intricate truths, sealed away in limestone, switch and corridor.

Oh wait. That's Scala Ad Caelum...

Beautiful. The soundtrack of Man.

stories.author: @cfalcon8342
stories.text:
So I have never played a single Kingdom Hearts game myself, but my best friend played all of them. She was so excited when KH3 came out, she was extatic for months, and later cried and vented to me about the ending. I really tried to read into it, learn about the plot of KH so we could have some more things to talk about, well, I figured out that understanding KH lore is quite a daunting task. I still don’t know everything, but i know barely enough to get the rough idea of it. Well, a few months later, in august, my friend passed away from her leukemia at 15 after 3 years of fighting. it was a small funeral, with many beautiful blue flowers, we were handed a schedule of the ceremony. The first song to play was one that she had chosen herself.
“Don’t think twice” by Hikaru Utada. I had never heard it before then, i only knew Dearly beloved, but now i can only think of her when I listen to this song.
I miss you Elina.
2004-2019.
Edit: I just want to thank you for all the kind comments, i read every single one.

stories.author: @JourneyofShadows
stories.text:
When I started my quest in this game seventeen years ago, I had no idea what I was going to get into.  This series has grown with me... and now here I am, on the brink of turning twenty-four, and am about to take part in the turning point of one of the greatest games of all time.  I've learned patience; I've learned pain; but most importantly, I've learned to never give up no matter the odds... But I'm not the only one who's had to learn these important lessons.  Everyone who's picked up a controller and played Kingdom Hearts has known these lessons, and there's no doubt in my mind that everyone's taken them to heart, like myself.

Thank you for the seventeen years of magic, Kingdom Hearts.  I'm hoping for another seventeen more after this final battle against Xehanort.

From a dearly beloved fan of the series.

stories.author: @thedude3065
stories.text:
again and again the number XIII returns
look at the cover for KHIII
Sora, Riku, Kairi, Ventus, Terra, Aqua, Roxas, Axel, Xion, Micky, Donald, Goofy, and Namine
XIII people in total
Organization XIII
XIII pieces of Darkness
Kingdom Hearts creator/director Tesuya Nomura's Fabula Nova Crystalsis game, Final Fantasy Versus XIII announced the same year as KHII
XIII years passed by and it's name was lost in time in spite of main character Noctis fulfilling his adventure earning two titles that places him above all other Final Fantasy Characters, the King of Kings, and King of Light
Noctis we met in in 2006 sleeping on his throne, legs crossed, cheek on right hand
final mix cover art features Sora, awake on his throne, legs crossed, cheek on right hand 
we met Yozora and people remember, Versus XIII became something again, as opposed to remaining changed 
when we see Noctis again in 2011 he wakes up in the back seat of his car and gazes out his window
when we see Yozora again in Remind  he wakes up in the back seat of his car and gazes out his window
Yozora and Noctis, their names translate to "night sky"
in the night sky the moon shine brightest
the moon reshaped is Kingdom Hearts
the Master of Masters, the one who began the original keyblade war, and gave Xehanort the means to begin another, the one character that every happenstance in the entire saga can be traced back to
only when this character has his story finally told, only then can anything left unanswered be explained
he's is voiced by Ray Chase, a professional voice actor, one whose career was given notoriety with his role as none other than Noctis himself in Final Fantasy XV
being a king you see also makes you a master
if a king is a master
then could the king of kings be the master of masters?
Sora and Yozora, are they two halves meant to be whole?
together are the champions of the light, the one true king of light?
the tale left untold was given an oath to return by it's teller

stories.author: @chuumon95
stories.text:
I'm hoping KH4 will feature Kairi as the playable protagonist with Donald and Goofy serving as her partners just as they did with Sora. It's about time she graduated from damsel in distress to a hero in her own right. While Riku searches for Sora, Yen Sid instructs Kairi to visit different worlds and identify the new 7 hearts after Maleficent and Pete steal a Gummiphone and gives it to Pete's old friend Emil Eagle to see if the data inside will be any good to them. At the same time they also try to find info on the masked people (the lost Masters of course) they saw Xigbar with before they take the Black Box from him. In case Mleficent decides to go after the other princesses, Yen Sid orders Terra, Ventus, Aqua, Roxas, Xion, and Axel to guard Snow White, Cinderella, Aurora, Alice, Belle, and Jasmine respectively. Since it will be her first time traveling through the worlds, Donald, Goofy, and Jiminy decide to go with her to watch her back. As for Mickey, he's tasked with following aleficent and Pete. This mission will serve as Kairi’s Mark of Mastery. Before she starts her journey, each character bestows Kairi a magic ability: Fire (Axel), Blizzard (Isa), Thunder (Roxas), Magnet (Xion), Earth or Gravity (Terra), Water (Aqua), Aero (Ventus), Cure (Namine), and Stop (Mickey).

The worlds Kairi visits will be based on these movies and in the following order:

Brave 
Frozen 2
Cinderella 3
The Little Mermaid 2
Pocahontas
The Princess & The Frog
Mulan 2
Moana
Aladdin & The King Of Thieves
Winnie The Pooh (2011) 

The worlds for Tangled the series and Snow White would also be visited but only in cutscenes. Radiant Garden and the Bug Blocks will return. Pocahontas, Tiana, Anna, Rapunzel, and Moana will be confirmed to be 5 of the new hearts. There will also be 6 summons: Olaf, Fairy Godmother, Maui, Genie, Mushu, and the 7 Dwarfs. During all this time, there will be cutscenes of Sora and Riku's time in Quadratum and after clearing all the Disney worlds, Kairi, Donald, and Goofy find their way there and join up with them for the final battles.

Towards the end, everyone learns a startling truth. When the X-Blade was broken into 7 lights and 13 darknesses, not only did the 7 lights become the hearts for the 7 Princesses, but the 13 darknesses became the hearts for 13 of the most black hearted villains, the 13 Lords of Darkness. And all of them must be reunited to recreate the X-Blade. 

I also came up with 2 side games:

First there is "KH: Mickey's Quest". This game takes place during the first. It will focus on what Mickey was doing while Goofy and Donald were traveling with Sora. The worlds Mickey visits are based on Gummi Bears, Leroy & Stitch, Bambi 2, Song of the South, The Wind In The Willows, Bedknobs & Broomsticks, Darkwing Duck, and The Great Mouse Detective.

The second is "KH: Bonds of Time" which will follow Roxas and Xion going on a special mission together. This will take place either before or after KH4. Yen Sid has the two of them go back in time to the days of the lost masters to learn more about them and their successors, 2 of whom they recognize as Ventus and Marluxia. Before they arrive in Daybreak Town, they travel to different times in various worlds. The worlds they visit are based on: Beauty & The Beast, The Sword In The Stone, The Hunchback Of Notre Dame 2
, Tarzan 2, Alice In Wonderland, The Lion King, The Little Mermaid 3, 101 Dalmations, and Ducktales The Movie: Treasure Of The Lost Lamp. I chose these movies so we can see their worlds done right with the new graphics and all and we can interact with the young version of Tarzan and Simba. We will also get to fight Gaston, Madam Mim, Cruella, and Merlock. Jiminy procures the aid of Bernard and Miss Bianca from "The Rescuers" to join Roxas and Xion to watch their backs and chronicle their journey on his behalf using the Gummi Phones. The gameplay for this game will be similar to Birth By Sleep only you don't have to create 3 games for 3 separate characters. Instead the player will be able to switch between Roxas and Xion during the journey and battles. Plus if one gets knocked out, the player will automatically be able to switch to the other and heal them when they can. Although both characters can be used, some abilities and techniques will be exclusive to each of them as they level up.

However, if KH4 is going to once again have Sora as the playing character. I hope at least 9 to 10 of these movies will be featured as new worlds. 

1.	THE SWORD IN THE STONE
2.	THE JUNGLE BOOK / 2
3.	ROBIN HOOD
4.	THE BLACK CAULDRON
5.	THE GREAT MOUSE DETECTIVE
6.	DUCKTALES THE MOVIE TREASURE OF THE LOST LAMP
7.	POCAHONTAS
8.	A BUG’S LIFE
9.	DINOSAUR
10.	THE EMPEROR’S NEW GROOVE
11.	ATLANTIS THE LOST EMPIRE
12.	TREASURE PLANET
13.	THE INCREDIBLES
14.	CARS
15.	CHRONICLES OF NARNIA: THE LION, THE WITCH, & THE WARDROBE
16.	THE PRINCESS & THE FROG
17.	BRAVE
18.	ZOOTOPIA
19.	MOANA
20.	GUMMI BEARS

So what does anyone else think? If anyone from Disney or Square-Enix is reading this, PLEASE ask Mr. Nomura to start making them.

stories.author: @devegas4910
stories.text:
So I realized why this song makes me so emotional: this is about a journey. 

In the first verse, we are introduced to someone in the state of dilemma. They’re asking themselves if they should take the risk “taste, what a bittersweet” makes it clear that this is something they’ve wanted but at the same time, they’ll be forced to leave behind what they love in order to achieve it. 

The hook makes it clear that they’re afraid of what it is that they want for many reasons. The losses, the failures, the many times they’ll fall down and feel broken. “It won’t be long, I’m almost here” is what keeps them going. Even through the tears. 

The second verse is drastically different from the first. Not different in how the lyrics are arranged, but in how the person has grown from their initial state of fear. It’s in no way over, but they’ve become more confident and self assured. They’re not afraid of the outcome anymore and are willing to risk everything now. 

Throughout the song, the instrumental demonstrates the path the person decides to walk. The heavy bass and dubstep is the chaos of the journey itself as it’s hard hitting and unpredictable at times. The piano is the calm throughout the storm. 

As we get closer to the end of the song, the bridge gives them a final obstacle. They fight through it with all of their might though and as we get to hook being sung one last time, it represents the journey’s end. Whether you’ve interpreted the subject to have fallen or succeeded, they are still proud of their decision to move forward and make the sacrifice.

stories.author: @ATLAS_TELAMON
stories.text:
Kingdom Hearts has always occupied an interesting space in my mind. In the dichotomy of: 'emotional, fun game' and 'loosely thrown together plot-hole fest', people tend to fall squarely on one side or the other. Personally, I think I'm on the fence. I grew up with these games, yet I'm intimately aware of what all these titles do wrong. Lately, I can barely play any of the games except for 1 simply because of all the problems I can't help but see with them. Why is it then, that I can't listen to this music without breaking into a sobbing fit? After all, KH3 released years after my cynicism regarding the franchise was solidified; I even found the game itself wanting. But despite the unrewarding gameplay, the refusal to break from the relatively familiar; I couldn't help but sob for fifteen minutes straight after the finale. Further, I know I'll be purchasing the DLC the day it comes out. Why? I know that, logically speaking, I won't find it any more fun than I did the base game. 


Because Kingdom Hearts is mine. In my unique human experience, where constant things are so rare and ephemeral.. Kingdom Hearts has been a constant. Even now, as an adult, it's still there. Every time I play any of the games, the feeling I felt when I was a child is, for just a moment, recalled. My cynicism is briefly dispelled as the opening sequences play. Some would call this nostalgia; I would call it more than that. It's an unexplainable thing; like the idea of seeing a dead family member, or a friend you never thought you'd see again. I never expect to boot up these games and feel anything other than disappointment. Yet I do. I feel happy and melancholic to the point of tears, without fail.


That's why I cry when I play Kingdom Hearts. That's why I support it so feverishly, even though I know how flawed it really is. Kingdom Hearts doesn't make me feel like I'm a kid again.


For just a second, it MAKES me a kid again.

stories.author: @jtotheroc
stories.text: I had to pull my car over to write this. I think as with any other fan of kingdoms hearts who have been with the series since the very beginning, we become very emotional with this song. For the majority of us, we were teenagers when the first one released, and now we're in our early 30- mid 30s when KH3 released. For me, I get very sentimental listening to this song and being fortunate to experience Sora and companies story since release. Been waiting for KH3 since finishing KH2 back in 2005, and it finally came 15 years later, and now, I have to say goodbye to this series, and I honestly didn't want it to end. I think this song is the best song in the franchise, it if metaphorical for Soras relationship with all his friends, especially his (I hope) girlfriend, Kairi. As soon as this song started playing following the credits (and absolutely losing my shit when I saw axel, Roxas, Lea, and Xion sitting on the belltower) I couldn't stop bawling like a child, and this is coming from a 35 year old grown man with a 7 year old son, especially when everyone's playing on the beach, finally able to love free from the darkness that Xehenort brought into the world, and then we pan to Kairi and Sora, holding hands, finally able to be with one another after multiple games apart, and then Sora just vanishes (and that probably hurt the most). So yeah, this song is very sentimental to myself, as well as other kingdom hearts fans and that's why we get emotional whenever we hear/have to watch it. I've been KH3 now about 5 times, and I still cry like a baby when this song starts playing.

stories.author: @TheUltimateRare
stories.text:
I only ever asked for respect. I got nothing.. So now I sit here wondering.. how can I live with myself.. for trying to do everything and nothing on my own.. all at once.. by using the powers of nothingness, in other words.. doing nothing for the sake of a task... and also using even my own dreams to understand my life. I've grown pained. I've grown regretful of others. I stopped caring if I was happy. I stopped caring if I lived on. I started crossing the street without looking... Because I knew I wouldn't get hurt.. I started not caring what others thought of me.. because I called myself a hero for using my talents to simply live without them.

I did all I could, yet I got nothing for it. I was ok for a while.. but that's because it hasn't built up yet. As I grew older, I understood that I can not accept this anymore. I've used my dreams and my knowledge to control the future how i see fit.. I had everything I could ever want, so why is it... that I asked for respect? it's because I was bullied. Treated like crap my whole life. Never had a friend that lasted more than a couple years, at first.. I was fine. but it's only after I got something special that I understood just how hopeless and pointless everything else has been..

I had the ability to make my own path.. yet everyone was making the path dark and twisted. I had others trying to control my every action. we call these parents and teachers, I call them weakness and slave masters. Why? Because to me... I only knew bullying and hate. I never got anything I wanted from anyone else. So even the ones closest to me... I would always think they would regret being close to me. I always think they would leave me or hate me too. I don't believe in a Life alone. Nor do I believe in this world being stronger than my background, All I do is put up with people.. Thinking they can do something for me.. and yet they always backfire, because they never respected me.. enough is enough. I'm not putting up with this anymore. It's too much now.

I would rather die, than put up with anymore annoyance. I just needed someone to be with. I didn't care who it was... or how it goes about.. but this is just sad. All I did was protect what really matters, while everyone else thinks I'm just some random dude. Heh. that's fine. But if you must think of me wrong, then I'll do whatever I want. I have the right to act the way that I want to, if you'll just treat me like everyone else. No. No more pain.

No more regrets. Oh well.. I guess I can't get better from this illness then. All of these actions they took have made it incurable. that's a shame... I would have hoped I could live longer and not be killed by the very people who think I'm just fine. but by all means, keep messing with me if you wish..... I don't care about this life anymore.

stories.author: @Liex59
stories.text: I remember when I first got my hands on this game. I told my best friend I was gonna play it nonstop all weekend, nothing was gonna get in between me and Kingdom Hearts 3. stories.author: @saltedlemonjuice1172
stories.text: This song makes you think back on the long 14 years this game series has created. It is part of my childhood and maybe yours. You can’t help but cry and realize how far Kingdom Hearts has come and how everything lead up to the ending of Sora’s lost heart. It was battle long and hard fought for us as the gamers to experience this game with a beautiful story (with plot holes). It makes you reflect how Kingdom Hearts affected your life growing up. It’s something you need in a childhood. The song is nostalgic despite being new. It gives you the feeling of how everything lead up to this point, an ending that we must see through. This game series has aged well and so will we. That is why we will continue on to complete Kingdom Hearts and see the ending!
